What the official sources say

  • 70-25-202(1)(a): landlord must give the departing tenant a written list of rent due and damage/cleaning charges within 30 days after termination of tenancy or surrender, with payment of the remaining deposit. (MCA 70-25-202; source)
  • 70-25-202(1)(b): if after inspection there is no damage, no cleaning needed, no unpaid rent and no unpaid utilities, the deposit must be returned within 10 days. (MCA 70-25-202; source)
  • 70-25-203: a landlord who fails to give the written list forfeits all rights to withhold any deposit for damages or cleaning. (MCA 70-25-203; source)

What happens to a Montana tenant when the landlord sells the house?

The lease stays in place, and the buyer steps into the seller's position as landlord. Montana Code Annotated 70-26-102 gives a person who receives transferred real property on which rent is reserved the same remedies for rent, nonperformance of lease terms, waste or forfeiture that the seller had.

That rule is why a tenant cannot be removed simply because a sale is coming. A buyer who wants the house empty has to wait out the lease or use a termination route the law allows. A buyer who wants a rental can keep the tenant and the rent roll.

Montana also protects the seller once the sale is done. Under 70-24-304, a landlord who conveys the premises in a good faith sale to a bona fide purchaser is relieved of liability under the rental agreement and the Residential Landlord and Tenant Act for events occurring after written notice to the tenant of the conveyance. Unless otherwise agreed, the seller stays liable for all security recoverable by the tenant and for all prepaid rent.

In plain terms, send the tenant a written notice of the sale, and settle the deposit and any prepaid rent with the buyer at closing so the money follows the lease.

Which Montana laws govern a rental?

Most residential rentals fall under the Residential Landlord and Tenant Act of 1977, MCA Title 70, chapter 24, and the Residential Tenants' Security Deposits chapter, Title 70, chapter 25. The Montana courts website points landlords and tenants to those two laws, plus chapter 26 on landlord and tenant residential and commercial matters and the state's prohibited discriminatory practices statute in Title 49.

Chapter 25 applies to all rentals of dwellings subject to Title 70, chapter 24, or chapter 33, which covers mobile home lots. Federal fair housing law applies on top of the state rules.

LawSubject
MCA Title 70, chapter 24Residential Landlord and Tenant Act of 1977
MCA Title 70, chapter 25Residential tenants' security deposits
MCA Title 70, chapter 26Landlord and tenant, residential and commercial
MCA Title 49, chapter 2, part 3Prohibited discriminatory practices
42 U.S. Code, chapter 45Federal fair housing

The Montana Judicial Branch hosts a landlord handbook of 31 pages and a tenant handbook of 29 pages, along with forms, on its landlord and tenant page. Both sides can read them without paying anything.

How much notice does a landlord have to give to end a Montana tenancy?

It depends on the reason. For a month-to-month tenancy, either side may end it with at least 30 days' written notice under 70-24-441, and for week-to-week the notice is 7 days. For a breach by the tenant, 70-24-422 sets shorter and varied periods.

  • Unpaid rent: the tenant has 3 days after written notice of nonpayment and of the landlord's intent to terminate to pay.
  • Unauthorized pet: 3 days.
  • Unauthorized people living in the unit: 3 days.
  • Most other noncompliance: 14 days, and the lease does not end if the tenant fixes the problem before the date in the notice.
  • Same breach repeated within 6 months: at least 5 days' written notice.
  • Verbal abuse of the landlord, or damage or danger to the premises or neighbors: 3 days.

The statute says a landlord who uses the 30-day month-to-month notice is not bound by the breach rules in 70-24-422. Acceptance of full rent due waives a claimed breach only when the claimed breach is nonpayment, according to 70-24-423.

The notice must be in writing and specify the acts or omissions. Follow the statute closely when a sale is waiting on possession.

How does a Montana landlord evict, and where are the forms?

If the tenant does not leave after a valid notice, the landlord files an action for possession in court. The Montana courts site offers a Notice to Vacate, an Action for Possession packet for asking the court to evict, a Writ of Assistance form, and a letter for notifying a tenant of additional cleaning after move-out.

Under 70-24-427, once a rental agreement is terminated the landlord has a claim for possession, rent and damages. Under 70-24-422(5), a landlord may recover actual damages and seek an injunction for a tenant's noncompliance, and may recover treble damages if the noncompliance is purposeful, though not for early termination of the tenancy.

Montana does not allow a landlord to retaliate. Under 70-24-431, a landlord may not raise rent, cut services or threaten a possession action because the tenant complained to a housing-code agency, complained in writing about a violation, or joined a tenant organization. A landlord who tries to clear a house for a sale right after a repair complaint should expect that issue to come up.

The courts' Court Help Program, reached at (406) 841-2975, and the Montana Legal Services HelpLine at 1-800-666-6899 are listed by the Montana courts among legal help resources. The Court Help Program offers free assistance on common civil legal issues.

What deposit and entry rules apply while a sale is pending?

Showing the house is allowed, but entry rules still apply. The landlord must give at least 24 hours' notice to enter, except in an emergency or when it is impracticable, and may enter only at reasonable times. A seller with a photographer, appraiser or buyer's inspector scheduled should plan around that notice.

The deposit rules matter just as much. The statute 70-25-102 applies chapter 25 to covered dwellings, and 70-25-206 requires a statement of the condition of the premises at the start of a lease. At the end of a tenancy the landlord has 30 days to deliver the written list of charges with any balance, or 10 days where nothing is owed. A landlord who misses the list forfeits the right to withhold for damage or cleaning.

  • Get the deposit amount and the move-in condition statement into the sale file.
  • Decide in the purchase contract whether the deposit transfers to the buyer or is credited at closing.
  • Keep copies of the written notice of conveyance you send the tenant.

Does a tenant change how a rental sells for cash?

Yes, because the occupancy, rent level and lease end date set the price a buyer can pay. A tenant-occupied house is bought as an income property or as a future empty house, and the offer reflects which.

Cash buyers can take the house with the tenant in place, so you do not have to rush a move-out or pay for repairs before closing. If you would rather deliver the house empty, the notice periods above are the lawful way to do it, and a month-to-month tenancy needs the 30 days.

The tax side can help a seller explain the numbers. The Montana Department of Revenue Long-Term Rental Reduced Rate applies to a property rented for 28 or more days at a time, for at least seven months of the year, as the tenant's residence. Short-term rentals, such as vacation rentals, and second homes fall under the flat 1.90% rate for 2026, so rental use changes what a new owner pays in tax.

Cash Home Buyers can review a Montana rental and give a written cash offer. We give general information here, not legal advice, so use the court forms or an attorney for any notice you plan to serve.

More questions about Montana Landlord Tenant Law and Tenant Rights

Can a Montana landlord end a lease early because the house is being sold?

Not by itself. A buyer takes over the landlord's rights under the existing lease, so the tenant stays until the lease ends or a lawful termination applies. For a month-to-month tenancy, either side can end it with at least 30 days' written notice under MCA 70-24-441.

How many days does a Montana tenant have to pay rent after a notice?

Three days after written notice of nonpayment and of the landlord's intention to terminate the agreement. If the tenant does not pay within that period, the landlord may terminate and the tenant must vacate under MCA 70-24-422.

Who keeps the security deposit when a Montana rental sells?

The selling landlord stays liable to the tenant for security recoverable under Title 70, chapter 25, and for prepaid rent, unless otherwise agreed. Sellers usually settle that with the buyer at closing so the funds follow the lease.

How much notice must a Montana landlord give before entering a rental?

At least 24 hours, except in an emergency or when notice is impracticable, and entry must be at reasonable times under MCA 70-24-312.

Where can a Montana landlord find eviction forms?

The Montana Judicial Branch landlord and tenant page provides a Notice to Vacate, an Action for Possession packet, a Writ of Assistance form and a landlord handbook.

What the official sources say

  • 72-2-112: surviving spouse takes the entire intestate estate if no descendant or parent survives, or if all decedent's descendants are also the spouse's; first $300,000 plus 3/4 of balance if only a parent survives; first $150,000 plus 1/2 of balance if some decedent's descendants are not the spouse's. (MCA 72-2-112; source)
  • 72-3-1101: small estate affidavit for personal property - probate estate (less liens) not over $100,000, 30 days since death, no personal representative application pending. (MCA 72-3-1101; source)
Selling in Montana?

How does probate work in Montana?

Montana follows the Uniform Probate Code, which means an estate can go through an informal or a formal process. The Montana courts website defines probate as settling the estate of a deceased person: gathering and managing property, paying debts and taxes, and distributing what remains to the people entitled to it.

The work is done by a personal representative, who may also be called an administrator or executor. The courts say the right process depends on the value of the estate and whether the person left a valid will. The Montana Judicial Branch offers a probate questionnaire that points you toward the likely route.

For anyone selling an inherited house, the key point is that someone must have legal authority to sign the deed. In an informal appointment, the clerk handles the application. Under MCA 72-3-225, the clerk may make the appointment effective once at least 120 hours have passed since the decedent's death, after making the findings required by 72-3-222.

StepWhat the statute or court says
Start the caseInformal or formal proceeding, generally within 3 years of death (72-3-122)
AppointmentClerk may act once 120 hours have passed since death (72-3-225)
Creditor noticePublished once a week for 3 weeks, with 4 months to present claims (72-3-801)
Close the estateSworn statement no earlier than 6 months after appointment (72-3-1004)

Is there a deadline to open a Montana probate?

Generally yes: no informal or formal probate or appointment proceeding may be started more than 3 years after the decedent's death. That is the rule in MCA 72-3-122, and it has exceptions, so an old inherited house is not necessarily stuck.

The statute allows a later informal appointment or formal proceeding if no proceedings about the succession or estate administration happened within the 3-year period. In that case the personal representative has no right to possess estate assets beyond what is needed to confirm title in the successors, and claims other than administration expenses cannot be presented against the estate. A will contest can be started within the later of 12 months from the informal probate or 3 years from the death.

Montana's three-year window is a good reason to act early on a house that is sitting empty after a death. A house with no one in authority cannot be sold, and it still collects property tax, insurance cost and wear.

Who has authority to sell an inherited house in Montana?

A personal representative can sell, mortgage or lease estate property, including land, at public or private sale, unless the will or a court order restricts it. That power comes from MCA 72-3-613, and a title company will want proof of that authority before closing.

Montana also lets the house stay with the family during administration. Under 72-3-606, real property may be left with, or surrendered to, the person presumptively entitled to it unless the personal representative decides possession is necessary for administration. The same section requires the personal representative to pay taxes and take reasonable steps to manage, protect and preserve the estate.

  • With a will: the named executor applies for appointment, then follows the will's terms.
  • Without a will: heirs under the intestacy statutes apply, and the court or clerk appoints someone.
  • With a joint tenant or a recorded beneficiary deed: the house may pass outside probate. The courts site links to a transfer on death deed form under MCA 72-6-415.
  • Held in joint tenancy or a life estate: Montana State University Extension publishes a guide on transferring such real property without probate.

What claims and deadlines do heirs face before the house is sold?

After appointment, the personal representative publishes a notice once a week for three successive weeks in a county newspaper, naming the appointment and address and telling creditors to present claims within 4 months of first publication or be forever barred. This is MCA 72-3-801. The personal representative may also mail notice to known creditors, who get the later of 4 months from publication or 30 days from the mailing.

Claims that would otherwise survive are barred against the estate unless presented within the earlier of 1 year after death or the time set by the notice, according to 72-3-803. That helps heirs and buyers see when the estate's debt picture settles.

Under 72-3-1004, a personal representative may close an estate by filing a verified statement no earlier than 6 months after the original appointment. It must state that the claims period has expired, that claims, expenses and taxes have been paid or arranged, and that a copy has gone to distributees and known creditors. If no proceedings involving the personal representative are pending 1 year after the statement is filed, the appointment ends.

A sale of the house can happen before closing. Proceeds usually pass through the estate, so confirm with the attorney or the court file who receives the net money and when.

What does selling an inherited Montana house for cash look like?

A cash sale works as a normal sale with a short closing timeline: the buyer pays cash, the personal representative signs the deed under the letters of appointment, and the title company records it. You do not need to repair, clean out or stage the house first.

Common snags include these: a will has not been admitted yet, heirs disagree, the house sits empty through winter, or taxes are behind. Property taxes keep running on a house in probate, with half due November 30 and half due May 31 each year, and a delinquency adds interest and a 2% penalty under MCA 15-16-102.

  • Gather the death certificate, will if any, and the letters of appointment.
  • Get the current tax balance from the county treasurer.
  • List heirs and their contact information so everyone can sign off on the price.
  • Photograph the property and note repairs, so the offer reflects its real condition.

Cash Home Buyers can give a written offer on an inherited Montana house and work around the court timeline. This page is general information, not legal advice, and a probate attorney or the clerk of court can confirm the right process.

Where can Montana families get free or low-cost probate help?

The Montana courts list several places to start. The Court Help Program at (406) 841-2975 gives free assistance on common civil legal issues, and it notes that probate is among the issues the program commonly sees. The Legal Service Developer Program at the Department of Public Health and Human Services can be reached at 1-800-332-2272. Montana Legal Services Association runs a HelpLine and intake line at 1-800-666-6899, Monday through Friday, 9:00 am to 1:00 pm, for low-income Montanans with pressing civil legal needs. The State Bar of Montana operates a lawyer referral service at (406) 449-6577.

The courts site also provides an affidavit of death, a small estate packet, and an affidavit for collection of personal property packet.

More questions about Montana Probate Laws

How long do I have to start a probate in Montana?

Generally 3 years from the date of death under MCA 72-3-122. There are exceptions, including late appointment when no proceedings occurred in that period, but a personal representative then has limited rights over estate assets.

Can I sell a house in Montana before probate is finished?

A personal representative with appointment can sell estate real property at public or private sale unless the will or a court order restricts it (MCA 72-3-613). Without an appointed personal representative or another valid transfer, no one has clear authority to sign the deed.

How long do creditors have to file claims against a Montana estate?

The published notice gives creditors 4 months from first publication, or 30 days from mailed notice if later for those who receive it. Under 72-3-803, claims are also barred 1 year after death when that comes first.

Does the house have to stay with the personal representative during probate?

No. Under MCA 72-3-606, real property may be left with the person presumptively entitled to it unless the personal representative finds possession necessary for administration.

When can a Montana personal representative close the estate?

By filing a verified statement no earlier than 6 months after original appointment, once the creditor claims period has expired and the estate has been administered, under MCA 72-3-1004.
